scenario_summary: Exploring counting principles using abstract mathematical sets and geometric shapes.
visual_setting: A clean, dark background with mathematical notation and geometric primitives.

scenes.title: Introduction to Counting
scenes.narration: Imagine you have a set of 3 shirts and 2 pants. How many different outfits can you make?
scenes.animation_description: Three shirts and two pants are displayed as nodes. Arrows connect each shirt to each pant, showing all possible combinations.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `Dot` for shirts and pants, and `Line` to connect them.

scenes.title: Counting Principle
scenes.narration: Each shirt can be paired with each pant. So, if you have 3 shirts, you can make 3 x 2 = 6 outfits.
scenes.animation_description: A formula 3 x 2 = 6 appears on the screen. An arrow points to the formula, highlighting the multiplication.

scenes.title: Generalizing the Principle
scenes.narration: This principle works for any number of items. If you have n shirts and m pants, you can make n x m outfits.
scenes.animation_description: Variables n and m are introduced, and a formula n x m = x appears. An arrow points to the formula, highlighting the general principle.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `MathTex` to display variables and formulas.

scenes.title: Applying to Larger Sets
scenes.narration: Let's apply this to a larger set. Imagine you have 5 different books and 4 different bookmarks. How many ways can you choose one book and one bookmark?
scenes.animation_description: Five books and four bookmarks are displayed as nodes. Arrows connect each book to each bookmark, showing all possible combinations.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `Dot` for books and bookmarks, and `Line` to connect them.

scenes.title: Calculating Larger Combinations
scenes.narration: For 5 books and 4 bookmarks, you can make 5 x 4 = 20 different combinations.
scenes.animation_description: A formula 5 x 4 = 20 appears on the screen. An arrow points to the formula, highlighting the multiplication.

scenes.title: Recap and Generalization
scenes.narration: In summary, the counting principle states that if you have n items and m items, you can make n x m different combinations.
scenes.animation_description: A recap of the formula n x m = x is displayed. The principle is repeated with different values for n and m.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `MathTex` to display the formula and recap.
